nice_guideline_used: NG136 (Hypertension in adults) + CG62 (Aspirin in pregnancy) + CG181 (Metformin in pregnancy) + standard anemia guidance

medications.dose: 100 mg twice daily (BID) – titrate by 100 mg BID every 2‑3 days to target <140/90 mmHg, max ≈200 mg three times daily
medications.duration: Titrate to target over 1‑2 weeks, then lifelong – review each trimester
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends labetalol as a preferred first‑line antihypertensive in pregnancy (safe in all trimesters) and CG62 advises antihypertensive therapy when BP ≥150/100 mmHg

medications.dose: 75 mg once daily in the evening
medications.purpose: Preeclampsia prophylaxis in a woman with chronic hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG62 recommends low‑dose aspirin 75 mg daily from 12 weeks gestation for women with chronic hypertension to reduce pre‑eclampsia risk

medications.medication: Ferrous sulphate 200 mg (≈65 mg elemental iron) oral tablet
medications.dose: 1 tablet once daily with vitamin C, separate from other meds by ≥2 hours
medications.purpose: Treat moderate iron‑deficiency anaemia in pregnancy
medications.nice_justification: NICE guidance on anaemia in pregnancy recommends oral iron replacement as first‑line therapy

medications.dose: 500 mg every 6 hours as needed (max 4 g/day)
medications.duration: As needed, review pain control weekly
medications.purpose: Replace NSAID and opioid for chronic low‑back pain, safer in pregnancy
medications.nice_justification: NICE pain management guidance advises paracetamol as first‑line analgesic in pregnancy

interactions_checked.interaction: Beta‑blocker may potentiate opioid‑induced sedation and respiratory depression
interactions_checked.action: Monitor for excessive drowsiness; consider tapering oxycodone and using acetaminophen alone

interactions_checked.interaction: Iron can reduce oral absorption of labetalol
interactions_checked.action: Take iron at least 2 hours apart from labetalol

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive gastrointestinal irritation and increased risk of fetal renal impairment

contraindications.reason: ACE inhibitor is teratogenic and contraindicated in pregnancy (NICE NG136)
contraindications.alternative: Labetalol or nifedipine as first‑line antihypertensive in pregnancy

contraindications.reason: NSAIDs are contraindicated in pregnancy due to risk of fetal renal impairment and oligohydramnios, and they interact with ACE‑I (triple‑whammy) (NICE CG62)

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed >60 mL/min/1.73 m² based on creatinine 1.1 mg/dL; will obtain formal eGFR before any renally cleared drug (e.g., metformin).
Serum potassium not available – will check before any future RAAS‑blocking agent.
Gestational age not documented – assumed >12 weeks (required for aspirin prophylaxis). Will confirm gestation.
Allergy status unknown – will verify no β‑blocker or iron allergy.
BMI, weight, and smoking status not recorded – needed for full cardiovascular risk assessment.
Urine protein/albumin not measured – will screen for proteinuria to assess pre‑eclampsia risk.
Fetal monitoring data not provided – coordinate with obstetrics for ultrasound and Doppler assessments.
treatment_summary: Stop lisinopril and ibuprofen immediately. Initiate labetalol 100 mg BID with titration to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg, add low‑dose aspirin 75 mg daily for pre‑eclampsia prophylaxis, start oral iron for anaemia, and replace opioid/NSAID pain regimen with acetaminophen as needed. Monitor blood pressure weekly, renal function and electrolytes after medication changes, and reassess haemoglobin after 3 months. Coordinate care with obstetrics for fetal surveillance and with pain services for non‑pharmacological pain management.
